rubric.title: Notes
rubric.lead: Short pieces about how this site is put together.

articles.title: A site made of blocks
articles.lead: An article is a list of blocks, the same ones a page is made of — so a writer never waits for a deployment to get a layout.

values.heading: Written in the panel
values.body:
This article was seeded by the command php artisan webx:demo, and it is an ordinary article: edit it, publish it, delete it.
Its content is blocks, which means the block types in the panel are what an article can be made of.

values.heading: Rubrics and tags
values.body: It sits in a rubric and carries two tags. A tag is in the index only once a rule has been written for its address, which is why an empty tag page never reaches a search engine.

articles.title: What comes next week
articles.lead: Dated ahead of time: the site answers 404 for it and the panel says «Scheduled» until the day arrives.

values.heading: A date instead of a scheduler
values.body: There is no job waiting to publish this. The date is the whole of it: before it the article is not on the site, after it it is.

articles.title: Addresses that survive a rename
articles.lead: Rename an article and its old address keeps answering — with a redirect to the new one, kept by the routing registry rather than by hand.

values.heading: One table of addresses
values.body: Every page, article and rubric takes its address from one registry. A rename writes the new address and keeps the old one as an alias, so a link somebody shared last year still arrives.

articles.title: Why an article has no template of its own, and why that is the reason it can look like anything
articles.lead: A title this long wraps on a phone and in a narrow card — which is the point of it being here.

values.heading: Blocks all the way down
values.body: The look of an article is the look of its blocks, and the look of a listing is the theme’s. Neither needs a template written for one article.

articles.title: A rubric is a shelf, a tag is a label
articles.lead: An article stands on one shelf first and may carry as many labels as it needs.

values.heading: Where it is found
values.body: The first rubric is the article’s main one: its trail and its address go through it. Tags only gather articles; an empty tag page never reaches a search engine.
